title: Bill Dillard and the first, second and third trumpet parts
summary: Dillard from Philadelphia played first trumpet, Red Allen was always the third hot man and Otis Johnson second in Russell's changing lineups.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Another trumpeter with the Luis Russell band was Bill Dillard.

Yes. A little boy from Philadelphia. Yeah, he was in Russell's band, come in as a first trumpet player. And he was very good, very good, really a very good musician. And he could really play the parts, too.
Yeah, Red was there while he was there.
Red was the third trumpet, then, and he was first?

Oh yeah. Red never played the first trumpet. In them days, they had first, second and third trumpet. The third trumpet was always the hot man. Of course, all of them could play. But the parts was written like that.
Well, now, when Otis Johnson was in the band...
Well, then, who did the first parts?

I don't know... Dillard, I guess. At one time there were three trumpets. I mean, I never knew exactly, but I know there were three trumpets in the band. And at one time there were two or three trombones. You see,
Russell had so many different versions of bands and things, it's hard to remember. And I was in and out so much. I was in and I was out, I was in and I was out -- one of them things.
